contradictions.detail: The listing specs say '6-Speed Manual Transmission', while the dealer description calls the car '2017 Toyota 86 Auto (Natl)' and refers to a 'seamless automatic transmission'. These are incompatible, and the manual requirement for this mission hinges on which is true.

critical_evidence.evidence: Nothing disclosed about track or autocross use. The aftermarket body kit, vented hood and lightweight-style wheels suggest an enthusiast owner, which raises the question but proves nothing.
No statement about an ECU tune, headers or intake. Exhaust tips look factory in the photos, but the engine bay was not examined here. CARB compliance is unknown.

The profile scopes NHTSA 21V587000 to 2018-2019 cars. This VIN decodes as a 2017. The tracker's recall list for this VIN shows only 17V295000 (spare tire) and 16V920000 (automatic/key-ignition cars only). Still confirm open recalls via a Toyota VIN lookup.

documentation.rationale: The identity half is present: VIN, a decode that agrees, a price stated to include all dealer fees, and a Carfax 1-owner and accident summary. The maintenance half is absent: no records, no repair documentation for the reported accident, and no photos of at-risk areas in this capture. The transmission contradiction undermines the listing's spec data.

condition.rationale: An accident or damage event is reported with no repair evidence. Photos show a non-factory front fascia and hood, badge-removal marks on the trunk lid and a small chip at the right headlight corner. No mechanical fault is stated, but nothing about the drivetrain, tires or underside is proven.

price_value.rationale: The $21,150 asking price is well above the $12,427-$16,781 fair-value range (mid $13,814) for an accident-reported, cosmetically modified base car. Active peers ask $18,500-$23,000, but the 860 SE and TRD Handling cars at that level are more desirable and unaccidented as far as known.

mission_fit.rationale: The FA20 86 is a named secondary bridge and the price sits under the ceiling. However, the manual is not confirmed because of the listing contradiction. Accident and aftermarket body work also hurt 6-24 month resale, which is central to a bridge.

logistics.rationale: Sacramento is a few hours' drive from Carmel and the seller is a California retail dealer, so smog and registration should be straightforward and a local PPI is plausible. PPI permission is not stated.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Base trim in common silver, with a non-factory front bumper and vented hood that read as an incoherent body-kit build rather than tasteful period modifications. A manual would be the one desirable trait, but it is unconfirmed.

seller_questions: Is this car a 6-speed manual or an automatic? Please send a photo of the shifter and of the door-jamb build label.

ppi_focus: Confirm the transmission type and clutch engagement point; check for slip, chatter and throwout-bearing noise.
Front structure behind the aftermarket fascia: radiator support, crash bar, frame-rail tips, headlight mounts; check weld and paint evidence.
Paint-meter all panels to map the accident repair; check the hood fit and latch.
OBD scan for codes, readiness monitors and ECU calibration ID to detect a tune; check for CARB EO labels on any intake or header parts.
Compression/leakdown and an oil-consumption question if any track use is suspected; look for oil seepage at the cam covers and front cover.
Cooling system: radiator condition behind the open lower grille, coolant level, fan operation.
Tires: date codes, brand match and inner-edge wear suggesting alignment issues after the accident.
Alignment readings and suspension for bent components from the front impact.
Airbag/SRS light status and seatbelt pretensioner function.
what_would_change_verdict: A shifter photo or VIN build data proving a 6-speed manual, plus a full history report showing a minor, cosmetic-only incident with a repair invoice.
A clean PPI showing undamaged front structure, a stock ECU calibration, sound clutch and fresh tires.
A substantial price reduction toward the fair-value range to reflect the accident and non-factory body parts.
Downward: confirmation that it is an automatic, an airbag deployment or structural damage on the report, or evidence of an undisclosed tune or track use.
evidence.mission_note: A first-gen 86 manual is a named secondary enthusiast bridge, but this listing cannot yet confirm the manual. The accident report and aftermarket front end also weaken the easy 6-24 month resale a bridge depends on.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes identity well: the VIN decodes cleanly to a 2017 Toyota 86 coupe, the price is stated to include all dealer fees, and the Carfax summary shows a single owner. It also discloses 'Accident or Damage Reported' with no repair details. The photos show a non-factory front fascia and vented hood, aftermarket wheels, removed rear badges with residual marks, and a small chip near the right headlight. That bodywork is consistent with, but does not prove, a front-end repair. The listing contradicts itself on the transmission, calling it a 6-speed manual in the specs and an automatic twice in the description. The asking price of $21,150 sits above the $12,427-$16,781 fair-value estimate. No service records, tune status, track-use disclosure, tire dates or interior photos were captured. The capture is thin, so these remain open questions rather than seller omissions.
evidence.next_action: Call Lending Group Auto and request a shifter photo, the full Carfax report with accident details, and confirmation that an independent PPI can be done in Sacramento before any deposit.
